ca_fence_boulder.blurb: Fence Boulder is one of the small bouldering stops at Humber Park in the San Jacinto Mountains above Idyllwild, at roughly 6,000 feet. It holds eight problems on a single block, and a short walk from the car gets you there. Most of the lines are gentle: four are in the very easy range, two sit at V0, one is V1, and there is a single V6 on the steep side of the boulder. The big slabby face is the draw for newer boulderers, while the shorter mantle problems on the opposite side add variety. The block is tonalite and it works well as a quick warm-up near the Tahquitz trailhead.

ca_flying_fortress_the.blurb: The Flying Fortress is a trad crag deep in the northern Wonderland of Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park, part of the Grey Giant group. Eight routes follow cracks on solid monzogranite, and the wall faces south, so it gets plenty of sun. Nearly everything is in the 5.10 range, with one easier line around 5.8 and a single 5.12 that is run out. You reach it by hiking in from the Willow Hole side, and the approaches in this group are long, so plan on a full day and bring a standard trad rack with cams and nuts.

ca_fun_house.blurb: Fun House is a small east-facing crag in the Inner Gorge of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop. It has eight routes on welded tuff, seven of them sport and one trad. Grades are concentrated between 5.10 and 5.11, with one easier line near 5.7, so it suits climbers warmed up on the moderate end of the gorge's range who want a few steady pitches. It sits about midway between the Central and Upper Gorge approaches, directly across the canyon from a better-known wall, and tends to see fewer climbers than the headline crags.

ca_gathering_wall_left_side.blurb: Gathering Wall - Left Side is the leftmost section of a low granodiorite wall in Rockview Park, in the Victorville area of the High Desert. Climbs here are short, and the section has eight routes split evenly between top rope and trad, ranging from about 5.4 up to 5.11. Several crack systems and boulders sit behind the bolted anchors, which makes it a handy place to practice gear placements and slung anchors before heading to taller cliffs. It lies directly behind the park's auditorium and overlooks the Mojave River.

ca_getaway_the.blurb: The Getaway is a northeast-facing sport crag on volcanic rock in the Box Canyon East section of New Jack City, in the High Desert near Barstow. It has eight bolted routes. A trio of easy lines starts the grade range around 5.3 to 5.8, then a cluster of four 5.10s forms the core, topped by one 5.11. Its position in the next canyon over from a few busier walls means a short uphill hike, and the aspect keeps it cooler than many crags nearby. Good for climbers working through the 5.10 grade.

ca_gold_eagle.blurb: Gold Eagle is a granodiorite dome on the Shuteye Ridge in the western Sierra Nevada, at around 8,300 feet. It is one of the Eagle domes around Shuteye Creek, and the wall sits next to a neighbouring dome that has its own routes. There are eight routes, six sport and two trad, mostly 5.10 to 5.11 with one 5.12, and at least one is two pitches. The hike in is long and the trail can be tricky to follow if you have not been before, so go with a clear plan and a companion who knows the way.

ca_harrison_boulder.blurb: Harrison Boulder is a small granite boulder on Mt. Rubidoux in Riverside, in the Half Moon area. It has eight lines, and the rock has good texture with cool edges. The faces are steep and often in shade, and the height is modest. Many of the lines are climbed on a top rope rather than as boulder problems, with the V5 being the main reason boulderers visit. The rest are mostly VB to V1, so it works for a short session with a mix of easy problems and one standout hard one.
